description: A user-friendly web application or dashboard that converts NASA satellite data into meaningful agricultural insights, helping farmers improve crop planning, reduce losses, and develop climate-resilient farming practices.
summary:
RootSphere: NASA-Powered AI for Intelligent Crop Rotation and Climate-Resilient Agriculture

RootSphere is an AI-powered agricultural decision-support platform that uses NASA Earth observation data to help farmers make smarter crop rotation decisions. It integrates satellite and climate datasets, including NASA POWER, GPM, SMAP, and MODIS, to analyze weather patterns, rainfall, soil moisture, and vegetation health. Farmers can select their field location and explore data-driven crop rotation strategies suited to local environmental conditions.

The platform compares different crop rotation options and provides recommendations based on climate suitability, water availability, soil health, and long-term sustainability. It also explains the potential benefits and risks of each strategy, helping farmers make informed decisions.

RootSphere addresses the Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data challenge by transforming NASA's Earth observation data into practical agricultural insights. It is important because climate change, unpredictable rainfall, and declining soil health threaten agricultural productivity. By connecting space-based intelligence with farming decisions, RootSphere aims to support climate-resilient agriculture, improve soil sustainability, and promote better resource management.
details:
RootSphere – AI-Powered Crop Rotation Advisor

RootSphere is a web-based agricultural decision-support system designed to help farmers make informed crop rotation decisions using geographical information and real climate data.

The application allows farmers to select their agricultural land directly on an interactive satellite map by drawing a boundary or uploading a KML file. Using geographical coordinates, the system calculates the selected land area in acres and performs an initial land-structure verification using OpenStreetMap data to identify mapped buildings and infrastructure.

After selecting the land, farmers can choose between a two-season and three-season crop rotation cycle. RootSphere connects to NASA's POWER API (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources) to retrieve climate information, including temperature and precipitation data, based on the selected farm's geographical coordinates.

The system analyses the retrieved rainfall and temperature information and applies a climate-based recommendation mechanism to suggest suitable crops for different seasons. Depending on the rainfall conditions, it recommends crop combinations such as rice, sugarcane, pulses, maize, cotton, chickpeas, sesame, sunflower, sorghum, pearl millet, horse gram, and cluster beans.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

  • Helps farmers make climate-informed crop rotation decisions.
  • Encourages sustainable agricultural practices and soil fertility management.
  • Promotes the use of nitrogen-fixing crops such as black gram, green gram, and horse gram.
  • Supports better utilization of available rainfall and climatic conditions.
  • Provides geographical land-area calculation and farm selection.
  • Makes agricultural planning more accessible through a simple multilingual interface.

Technology Stack:

  • Programming Languages: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
  • Mapping: Leaflet.js and Google Satellite Map tiles.
  • Geospatial Processing: Turf.js for calculating land area and geographical centroids.
  • Land Verification: OpenStreetMap and Overpass API.
  • Climate Data: NASA POWER API.
  • File Support: KML file upload for importing farm boundaries.
  • Interface: Responsive web-based dashboard with English, Tamil, and Hindi language support.

Creativity and Innovation:

The main innovation of RootSphere is combining geographical farm selection, satellite-based visualization, NASA climate datasets, and crop rotation recommendations into a single agricultural planning platform. Instead of providing generic crop suggestions, it uses the geographical location of the selected farmland to retrieve relevant climate information and generate a seasonal crop rotation schedule.

The project also considers land area, rainfall conditions, temperature, seasonal crop suitability, soil fertility improvement, drought tolerance, and the number of growing seasons when generating recommendations.

RootSphere aims to bridge the gap between space-based climate information and practical agricultural decision-making, supporting more climate-resilient and sustainable farming communities.
